claims.summary:
The certificate cannot honestly be issued from this batch, so output/certificate.json was not written and the source records are untouched.

For b4 to be authorized three things must all hold: the copy b1 must capture the reissued child credential c3 (so b1 after c3), alpha must own the account when b1 is taken (b1 before a2 or after a3), and b4 must be delivered before c4 revokes the parent c2. None of those is fixed by the exports: b1 sits at the start of the delivery-service export, the only signed cross-service attestation is c2 before b4, and the recorded outcomes only pin c2 and a1 before c3, c3 before c4 before a4, and b2 outside the interval between a2 and a3. Ordering by logged_at would make the batch look clean, but those clocks are per-service. The proposed certificate therefore depends on unrecorded chronology. The customer needs to supply signed ordering evidence for those three relationships (or otherwise establish the actual order) before customer success can certify the batch.
